Guide
A quick reference to what this tool does and how to use each part. For internal use.
What this tool is

This app builds the business case for SAP solutions. For a chosen area you can (1) quantify the benefits and ROI, (2) build the investment / cost side — people, timeline and other costs, and (3) plan the implementation. It is used both with external prospects and as an internal working tool, so keep entries professional and accurate.

The five modules
  • Module 1 – HR & Recruitment: benefit & ROI calculator for SuccessFactors HR, recruitment and onboarding improvements.
  • Module 2 – Supply Chain & Logistics: benefit & ROI for supply-chain processes (with several sub-scenarios).
  • Module 3 – SAP Commercial Expansion: benefit & ROI for SD / global sales expansion.
  • Module 4 – Investment Case: the cost side — IT & Business resources (hours × grade rate), a visual timeline with phases, additional yearly costs, contingency mark-ups, and a cost breakdown by phase.
  • Module 5 – Project Management: the implementation plan per SAP edition (phases, sub-phases, activities), with resource planning you can view in hours or FTE.
How the tabs connect

The benefit modules (HR, Supply Chain, SAP Commercial) show ROI = their benefits versus the project’s investment. That investment number comes from the Investment Case. Inside the Investment Case, the Project type setting decides which module receives it:

  • Project type = HR → the Investment Case’s total cost per year flows into the HR tab’s break-even.
  • Project type = SAP Commercial Expansion → it flows into that tab’s break-even.
  • Project type = Default → it is not routed anywhere; pick HR or SAP Commercial to link it.

The amount that flows over is IT + Business resource cost (hours × grade rate × contingency) plus Additional Costs, per year.

Using the Investment Case
  • Project setup: choose the project type, duration and start date.
  • Resources: add IT and Business people into clusters (e.g. “Implementation team”). Each person picks a Grade (which sets the rate) and you enter hours per month. Use Add cluster to group people.
  • Copy & paste people: tick the checkbox on each row you want, click the copy icon (⧉) on any ticked row, then press the orange Paste button that appears on any cluster heading — in either the IT or Business table — to drop the copies in (you can paste into more than one cluster). Copies bring their hours along; the grade is kept when pasting within the same table and cleared when copying between IT and Business. When you’re finished, click the × beside a Paste button to clear the copied items and hide the orange marks. Works the same in Hours or FTE view.
  • Hours / FTE toggle: switch the grid between hours and FTE. FTE is based on working days (Mon–Fri) at 7.5 hours per day: in weeks view, 1 FTE = a full working week = 37.5 hours (5 × 7.5); in months view, 1 FTE = that month’s working days × 7.5, so it varies by month — e.g. a 22-working-day month is 165 hours, a 20-day month is 150 hours. Weekends don’t count, and because the underlying hours are the same, the FTE shown for the same work differs between weeks and months view. The summary column shows the average FTE across the periods a person is active.
  • Timeline & phases: paint which phases / sub-phases / activities are active each month. This drives the cost breakdown. You can switch the view between months and weeks and the painted phases follow the calendar — this requires a project start date to be set. In weeks view, columns are real Monday–Sunday calendar weeks, so the first week starts on the Monday on/before your start date and may include a couple of pre-start days (which carry no hours).
  • Per-person phase split: by default a person’s hours in a month are split evenly across the phases painted that month. Right-click a person’s hour cell to set a custom split (e.g. 80% Discover / 20% Prepare) — the counter must reach 100%.
  • Vacation weeks: in the section just under the timeline, click Add vacation period and pick a from–to week range (add as many periods as you like). Those weeks are shaded grey in the week view of both the timeline and the two resource tables. It is visual only — the cells stay editable and no hours, FTE or costs change — and the shading also appears in the Excel export.
  • Additional costs & contingency: add extra yearly costs; set IT / Business contingency % in Setup.
  • Cost breakdown: shows cost by phase, including contingency.
Using Project Management
  • Pick the SAP implementation type (edition) — each has its own phase plan.
  • Plan resources the same way (clusters, grades, hours).
  • Hours / FTE toggle: switch the grid between hours and FTE. FTE is based on working days (Mon–Fri) at 7.5 hours per day: in weeks view, 1 FTE = a full working week = 37.5 hours (5 × 7.5); in months view, 1 FTE = that month’s working days × 7.5, so it varies by month — e.g. a 22-working-day month is 165 hours, a 20-day month is 150 hours. Weekends don’t count, and because the underlying hours are the same, the FTE shown for the same work differs between weeks and months view. The summary column shows the average FTE across the periods a person is active.
  • Park and restore activities. This tab keeps its own data, separate from the Investment Case.
Settings panels
  • Parameters: view and edit the input parameters per area.
  • Benefits: the benefit categories / bars and their formulas.
  • Formulas: build and adjust the formulas behind the numbers.
  • Import / Export: save all customisations to a JSON file and load it back later.
  • Setup: currency, editable exchange rates (DKK per unit), contingency, grade rate cards, and the FTE basis.
Currency & exchange rates

Choose the display currency in Setup — everything converts automatically. You can edit the exchange rates (DKK per 1 EUR / USD / GBP) in Setup as well.

Excel export — what it can and can’t do

What it does:

  • The export is a fixed snapshot in one mode — either hours or FTE, depending on the “Export in FTE” checkbox you tick at export time. Unlike the app, there is no Hours/FTE toggle inside Excel; to switch, re-export with the checkbox set the other way.
  • Exports the full Investment Case (resources, timeline, additional costs, cost breakdown, rate card) as a live spreadsheet — most numbers are formulas that recalculate when you change hours or grades.
  • The cost breakdown reflects each person’s phase split.
  • You can re-import an exported file (Settings → Import / Export) to load changes back into the app, including custom splits.

How to edit it in Excel:

  • To add a person, copy an existing person’s whole row inside a cluster (so all the hidden formulas and the rate helper come along), then change the name, grade and hours.
  • The “Rate helper” column shows “↓ copy” — copy it down when you add rows. It carries each row’s rate, looked up from the grade. If a grade is mistyped it shows “grade misspelled” and that row’s cost goes to 0 — fix the grade.
  • Every resource row already has formulas for every year, so you can add hours in any year.

What it can’t do:

  • It can’t auto-create a new resource — you must copy a row. It can’t give a brand-new Excel person a custom phase split (do that in the app).
  • Structural changes (adding people / phases, custom splits) are best made in the app and re-exported.
  • Export needs an internet connection (it loads the Excel library online).
Good to know
  • The app always opens on the landing page.
  • Use “back it up” to make a safety copy of the file.
  • The structure checker may report a few harmless “duplicate ID” warnings — they don’t break anything.
